title: Add the ability to run a short filesystem test
description: Add a shortened version of the test that runs for about 5 minutes against local storage, rather than the 15 it takes to run the full test against the local EBS drive.

title: Add a Github action to validate changes
description: This github action can be used to indicate if a push will be successful

title: Add the ability to run fsbench in a shortened form
description: This addition allows you to run `make short` to run a shortened version of fsbench which completes in approximately 5 minutes against local EBS storage.

title: Update fsbench to R 4.4.0 and include an automated deployment script for Support/SE use
description: This PR updates and fixes fsbench to use R 4.4.0and renv 1.0.7 and resolves the currently broken nature of the R package dependency in this repo. Additionally, I've added a deployment script that automates much of the process of running this utility by allowing the user to enable this script to install the correct version of R, run fsbench, and then uninstall R on Redhat 8/9. and Ubuntu 22/20

title: Update fsbench to R 4.3.2 and renv 1.0.5, including deployment script
description: This PR updates and fixes fsbench to use R 4.3.2 and renv 1.0.5 and resolve the currently broken nature of the R package dependency in this repo. Additionally, I've added a deployment/deployment.sh script that automates much of the process of running this utility by allowing the user to enable this script to install the correct version of R, run fsbench, and then uninstall R on Redhat 8/9. and Ubuntu 22/20

title: Initial sketch for Rmd-style reporting
description: Currently, this requires @kevinhankens test results (aws-fsbench) to be in a sibling directory. We should curate that set and bundle them into this repo before merging.

title: Parallel tests fix + visualization improvements
description:
* Ensures that the parallel tests are actually marked as such to ensure they are graphed separately.
* Fixes test name widths to make them more readable
* Fix bug where 16x parallel tests would be marked/graphed separately due to bad regex
* Fix bug where reporting of invalid globs did not work correctly
* Minor theme improvements to make the graphs more readable

For the sample graphs and data, see the `examples` directory.

title: Update README.md to add usage of comparison tool
Add results comparison functionality
description:
Adds `compare.R` to compare multiple benchmark runs against different filesystems.

Example invocation:

`Rscript compare.R ssd=*ssd.csv efs=*efs.csv`

This will load all *ssd.csv and *efs.csv files. The runs for a particular filesystem are averaged together, and these averages are graphed. The final output is generated as an image file. This is done using `ggpubr` which has the unfortunate downside of pulling in an insane amount of dependencies.

Sample image created:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28230621/113451228-2f85b980-93c7-11eb-9b47-0f39b89509e8.png)

title: Added parallel tests using DD
description:
The `dd` utility was chosen here because it is heavily optimized and does not use much CPU, especially compared to similar utilities within R such as `fread`.  I wanted to minimize CPU usage as much as possible to ensure that the number of cores available on the machine did not become a limiting factor for the tests as more parallelism is used, thus ensuring the workload is truly IO bound.

These tests show that throughput for both EFS and EBS is limited and decreases (fairly) linearly when multiple tests are run simultaneously, as one would expect.

For latency, we parallelize small file tests, which show that these operations roughly decrease linearly as more clients are added as well. This makes sense, as we expect to be throughput constrained, and we expect that latency is fairly constant. However, it appears that many simultaneous writers performs exceptionally poorly on EFS compared to read performance which is quite good and tracks with EBS performance.
